No. The 67.7 ha loss was recorded in 2020, which is before the 2020-12-31 baseline, so it falls outside the post-cut-off period.

For 2021–2025, the evidence found no tree-cover loss event of 0.5 ha or more anywhere in the asset (ASSET-B, 2,843.1 ha). Hansen data covered the whole asset. The only post-baseline loss was 0.4 ha in 2021, in patches under 0.5 ha, which are not counted as events.

Other pre-baseline losses were 0.8 ha in 2008, 25.5 ha in 2015 and 4.8 ha in 2017. JRC maps 0 ha of forest in 2020.

Limits: this does not rule out all change, since small patches, edges or features narrower than the 30 m pixels may be missed. It is also not a regulatory or compliance finding, and it says nothing about periods outside 2021–2025.
